Subject: Pricing & committed-use options for SaaSBeta - post-call recap

Hi Alice / Bob,

Thanks again for the quick discovery today. Recap and next steps below so we have alignment: 

Call recap:
- Primary use case: real-time summarization + vector search for product help articles (latency-sensitive).
- Expected traffic pattern: 200k inference requests/day initially, trending toward 1.2M/day in 6-9 months.
- Token profile: average request ~1.2k input tokens, ~300 output tokens; estimated ~180M tokens/month now, 1.2B tokens/month at scale (see attached estimates).

Pricing / budget signals you shared:
- Initial annual budget target: $120k-$180k for pilot year (constrained).
- Long-term procurement target: budget for 1M+ monthly token volumes if product traction.
- You asked for target unit economics: looking for guidance on $/1M tokens and committed-use discounts.

What we propose to next: 
1) Marissa to send a follow-up with proposed committed-use tiers and startup program details (this email).
2) Alice to confirm which token projection tab in the attached file is the most realistic.
3) Scheduling: 30-min contract/pricing review the week of Apr 12 to discuss SOW and procurement timeline.

Proposed high-level numbers (initial ballpark to help budget conversations):
- Hosted list price (no commitment): $60 per 1M tokens (example for this workload).
- Startup program: 50% off list for qualifying startups for first 12 months => $30 / 1M tokens.
- Committed-use (12-month): tiered pricing by average monthly volume:
  - >= 10M/mo: $40 / 1M tokens
  - >= 50M/mo: $30 / 1M tokens
  - >= 200M/mo: $20 / 1M tokens
- Multi-year incentive: additional 10% off for 24-month committed deals (applies to committed-use rate).

Notes on unit economics and tradeoffs:
- Higher commitments allow deeper discounts and enable us to reserve Dedicated capacity for predictable latency.
- We can explore burst buffers and canary policies to keep costs low during ramp.

Attachments: SaaSBeta_Monthly_Token_Estimates.xlsx (please confirm tab).

Next steps: Alice -> confirm token projection tab; Marissa/Aditya -> send formal pricing tiers & SOW draft; schedule call.

Best,

Hi Alice / Bob — looping in a quick commercial proposal and answers to your questions. Marissa flagged your budget constraints; happy to see what we can do to structure a program that gets you started while preserving unit economics for Redwood.

Key answers: 
- Startup program + committed-use: We can stack the startup program for qualified customers with a limited committed-use discount for year 1. Typical structure: startup credit/discount applies first (e.g., 50% off for 12 months), then committed-use pricing applies after credits are exhausted or at renewal depending on contract language. We can also structure a blended priced committed-use if you prefer predictability.
- Minimum commit: We offer monthly minimums expressed as an annualized committed monthly average. A common pilot commit is 10M tokens/month (annualized) with a 12-month term; we can also do quarterly true-ups for ramp.
- Pro-rated credits: Yes, we can pro-rate startup credits during ramp if agreed in SOW.

Proposed committed-use tiers (blended committed rate, $ / 1M tokens):
- Pilot (10M/mo commit): $28 / 1M tokens (if startup program applies, blended effective ~$14 / 1M for year 1)
- Growth (50M/mo commit): $22 / 1M tokens (with startup credit year 1 => effective ~$11 / 1M)
- Scale (200M/mo commit): $15 / 1M tokens (with startup credit => effective ~$7.5 / 1M)

Multi-year incentives:
- 24-month committed deal: additional 10% off the committed-use rate (applies from signing date).
- 36-month: additional 15% off, subject to review.

Attachments: Proposed_SOW_v2.pdf — includes sample payment schedule, true-up mechanics, and termination/rollback protection.

Next recommended steps:
1) Marissa to send SOW + pricing sheet as a formal commercial package (we'll include blended numbers to match your budget constraint).
2) SaaSBeta to confirm preferred commit tier and timeframe (pilot vs growth) by Apr 19 so we can hold pricing.
3) Legal procurement: exchange initial redlines; we can accept short-form PO for pilots to speed onboarding.

Happy to hop on a short call this week if you want to walk through the SOW.

Regards,
Aditya Rao
